To all you players out there,@welcome to the world of Super Robot Wars!@I'm Arado Balanga!
And serving as my coach is the demon drill@instructor who makes crying kids laugh...
Why would they laugh?
Huh?
Whatever. I'm Major Kai Kitamura, leader@of the Special Combat Training Unit.
He may not look it, but the Major's actually@pretty young.
Ngh! What's that supposed to mean!?@You don't need to say that!
S-Sorry!
...Ahem.@Now, let's begin our lesson on how to play.
Y-Yes, sir! I'm counting on you!
Arado, have you ever played@Super Robot Wars before?
No, sir!@I'm a total rookie!
...I trust you've read the manual@cover to cover?
Nope! I'm going in totally blind!
You fool!@What do you take Super Robot Wars for?
A-A simulation RPG, sir!
...Hmm, that's correct.@Then I'll explain everything from the start.
U-Um, Major Kai...@I'm not so great at remembering stuff.@Will I be okay?
Then drill this into your head first.@If anything's unclear, press <I=92>.
<I=92>... you mean on the@wireless controller?
Right.@Depending on the situation, it'll explain@the controls and features.
When in doubt, <I=92>.@Don't forget that.
Roger!
Now, I'll explain step by step@how to play Super Robot Wars.
Scenes like this one, where we're talking,@are called Scenario Demos...
You advance the "Scenario Demo" by pressing <I=41>.
And pressing <I=55> and <I=41> together@fast-forwards it.
Furthermore, pressing <I=61> and <I=55> together@skips the "Scenario Demo" entirely.
All right, let's try it...
Wait. If you try it here, this Scenario Demo@will end.
Whoa... R-Right.@Close one, close one.
But that feature'll be handy@for second playthroughs and stuff,@so I'd better write it down.
Good attitude, but do you actually@remember exactly what I said?
Uh, um... well... er...@How did it go again?
...I thought so. In that case, press <I=45>.
That brings up the Backlog, which lets you@scroll back and reread the conversation@up to a certain point.
So it's fine even if I accidentally@skip past some lines!
However, there's a limit to how much you@can reread. Keep that in mind.
Roger that!
Also, sometimes words in a different@color will appear in the conversation...
That's called a "Keyword." Press <I=47>@to open a window that explains it.
<Inspector Incident>.@...Press <I=47> at times like this for an explanation.
<Inspector Incident>.@Press <I=47> and give it a try.
Got it?
Right!
For other controls in the "Scenario Demo,"@try pressing <I=92>, as I explained earlier.
That will display a panel@explaining the various controls.
Like this.
Gotcha...@So if I press <I=92>, I can see@that control guide again.
Now, let's move on to the battle map.
Hmm, so this is the battle map.
In Super Robot Wars, you progress by@clearing the battle map prepared@for each scenario.
First, you move your robots, known as "units,"@during the Player Phase...
Once you're done, the computer@moves the enemy units.
So my turn and the enemy's turn alternate.@Kinda like shogi or baseball, huh?
That's right.@The game proceeds by repeating@the Player Phase and Enemy Phase.
Got it.@So what am I actually supposed to do?
The task you must complete to clear a@scenario, the Mission Objective, is shown@under General Commands.
General Commands?
Put the cursor on a unit and press <I=41>@to bring up the "Individual Commands"@for controlling that unit...
Put the cursor where there's no unit and@press <I=41> to display the "General Commands."
Like so.
Now press <I=41>.
Gotcha...
And if I put the cursor on a unit and press <I=41>,@the "Individual Commands" come up, right?
Can I really memorize all those commands...?
Don't worry.@You'll understand how each command works@once you actually use it in the game.
The "Mission Objectives" you mentioned earlier@are under "General Commands," right?@Let's take a look.
That red robot is@the Razangriff Raven.
So I control that thing and@move it to the point?
Correct.@Get it to that designated point,@and you'll have met the victory condition.
Now, use the "Move" Unit Command@and head for the designated point.
Note that the Mass-Production Huckebein Mk-II@over there can't act this time.
Each unit can only act once per phase.
Once a unit finishes its action,@it can't move again that phase. Be careful.
Then let's begin@LESSON 1: Movement.
Huh?@Didn't quite make it...
All units that can move@have now finished their actions.
What now?
Hand the phase over to the enemy.@Select "End Phase" at the top of the@"General Commands" and confirm it.
Otherwise, the game won't progress.
What happens if I give the enemy the phase?
Normally, enemy units would act.@But since there are no enemies right now,@it'll go straight back to the player phase.
So that means it's my turn, right?
All right, this time I'll nail it!
Now, end the player phase.
That clears LESSON 1.
Next one, please!
Then let's move on to LESSON 2.
Same as before?
Not quite. The designated point is over there.
It's kinda far...@Well, I'll just get there in two moves.
Wait.@An "SR Point Condition" has been added@to the "Mission Objectives."
Seriously?@Show me that again, Major.
Yeah.
Hey, it's true.
"SR (Super Robot) Points"...@Each map has one task, separate from@the victory conditions.
Clear it, and you'll earn an "SR Point."
Is that actually good for anything?
The moment you get it, you receive "PP"...@points for training pilots. Each allied pilot@on the map gets 10.
Then I've gotta get them!
However, if you earn the points,@you'll be judged a skilled player,@and the game's difficulty will rise.
If you obtain 80% or more of all "SR Points"@(one per map), the difficulty becomes Hard.@Below 80%, it becomes Normal.
So beginners don't need to push themselves@to collect "SR Points." They have nothing@to do with scenario branching conditions.
So it's like a challenge for players@who think they've got skills, huh?
That's right.@That said, I recommend beginners choose@"Beginner's Mode" when starting the game.
Is there some difference?
Yes. The game's difficulty is locked@to "NORMAL" from start to finish.
So I don't have to worry about@the conditions for getting "SR Points"?
Correct. But earning an "SR Point" gives you@a flat bonus of funds. When you have@the leeway, give it a shot.
Then when it looks like I can grab@an "SR Point" easily, I'll go for it!
Now, let's sum up "SR Points."
But with that unit's movement,@there's no way I can reach the point@in a single move.
In that case, use Spirit Commands.
Spirit Commands?
They're special commands@assigned to each pilot.
By spending a pilot's "Spirit Points," or "SP,"@they can produce all sorts of effects@on units and pilots.
Wh-Whoa, sounds like magic.@Can I fire those off like crazy from the start?
Depends on the pilot.@Though at low levels, they'll only have@a limited set of Spirit Commands.
So when a pilot levels up...
Accordingly, they gradually learn@new Spirit Commands, and their@Spirit Points increase too.
Then if I learn around 100 Spirit Commands,@I'll be invincible!
Life doesn't work out that easily.@A single pilot can learn@up to six Spirit Commands.
Aw, c'mon...
When a new pilot joins you, check@which Spirit Commands they have.
You won't be able to clear LESSON 2@without using Spirit Commands.
Roger! I'll give it a shot!
All right!@Time to take on LESSON 2!
Before that, hand the phase over to the enemy.
H-How do I do that?
Select "End Phase" at the top of the General@Commands and press <I=41>.
Normally, the enemy units would act now.@But since there aren't any enemies,@it goes straight back to the Player Phase.
All right, I'm gonna give LESSON 2 my all!
Now use End Phase to end the@Player Phase.
Select "End Phase" from the General Commands@and press <I=41>.
Okay!@Now let's take another shot at LESSON 2!
Hold on.@You won't reach the target point without using@a certain something.
A certain something?@You mean Spirit Commands, sir?
Right. Use Accel, a Spirit Command@that raises a unit's movement.
There are also many other kinds of@Spirit Commands besides Accel.
Valor when you want to deal big damage,@Flash when you need to dodge for sure...
Vigor or Trust when you want to restore@a unit's HP...
Choosing the right Spirit Command for each@situation is the key to winning.
Then I'll just zip-zip-zip over there with@Accel and clear this thing!
Oh... You seem confident.
You bet!
If you fail...@you only get two refills at meals.
Gah!@B-But I'll roll the dice and give it a shot!
Your dice rolls never pay off.@Are you sure about this?
Actually... it'd be nice if I could@get a do-over if I mess up, heh...
That's what saving is for.
Saving?
Yes. In the command menu, there's a command@called Suspend Save.
Use it to record your progress@partway through the game.
And during the game, <I=61><I=53><I=55> (hold)...
...and you'll return to where you saved.
So, a soft reset, basically...
If you make a mistake you can't undo,@you can soft reset and try again.
Always save before the moments that count.
Got it, sir!@Now, on to LESSON 2!
All riiight, cleared it!
That earns you an SR Point.
Aw, man... I blew it.
If you'd used the Spirit Command Accel,@you should've reached the point.
Oh well. Just this once, I'll let you@have the SR Point.
I see.@So that's what getting an SR Point does.
The conditions for earning SR Points@vary from map to map.
Some are simple, like this one, while others@require you to make full use of various@skills and strategies.
Also, if you replay after a Game Over,@you can't earn the SR Point. Keep that in mind.
Th-That sounds kinda tough...
You can still progress through and clear@the game without earning SR Points.
So I recommend beginners play without@worrying about SR Points.
That keeps the game's difficulty lower, too.
Got it!@Then I'll take it easy and not worry about it!
Now, next up is combat.
Combat is arguably the most important element@of Super Robot Wars.
Then let's get right to it!
Don't rush, Arado.@You won't win battles by going it alone.
The key is making good use of your units.
Units, huh...
The units you control on the map come in@two types: Twin Units and Single Units.
A Twin Unit has two positions... a Main unit@that leads, and a Sub unit that follows it,@for a total of two machines...
A Single Unit consists of just one@machine: the Main unit.
A Twin Unit acts as a single group. Both@machines move together and attack together.
Also, only Twin Units can use@Twin Spirit Commands.
Only Main pilots can use Twin Spirit Commands.@Unlike regular Spirit Commands, they consume@the Spirit Points of both Main pilots.
...Perhaps it'd be easier to understand@if I showed you.
But there aren't any Twin Units on the map, sir.
You can reorganize units into Single Units@or Twin Units on the map, too.
How do I do that?
Use the Join unit command to combine two@Single Units within the surrounding 8 squares@into a Twin Unit.
There are no special requirements, like Will,@but battleships are the exception--they can't@form a Twin Unit.
The window shown when joining displays the@squad's Abilities and their effects.
Abilities?
Abilities are equipped to units and pilots,@granting special effects that give you an edge@in battle.
Units and pilots each have Slots that can@hold three Abilities apiece.
And when three or more of the same Ability@are equipped, an Ability Effect activates.
Ability Effects give a squad various bonuses,@such as increased weapon damage or evasion.
A Single Unit counts six Slots in total, from@its unit and main pilot, while a Twin Unit@counts twelve.
So a Single Unit can have up to two@Ability Effects, but...
A Twin Unit can activate up to four Ability@Effects for each unit, so it's a better deal!
You equip Abilities with the Ability command@during the intermission.
Now, let's try using a Twin Spirit Command.
When a Twin Unit attacks, the sub unit doesn't@have to attack, but it can still be targeted@by enemy counterattacks.
And as I said earlier, each unit can only act@once per phase, so the sub unit will also@finish its action.
It finishes its action without doing anything?@What a waste.
In that case, just split the Twin Unit@back into Single Units.
To turn a Twin Unit into Single Units,@use the Disband unit command.
But be careful: separating will cancel@the effects of any active Twin Spirit@Commands.
Now, I'll bring out some enemy units.
Before we get into combat, I'll explain weapons.
There are three types of weapons:@Normal, ALL, and MAP.
Um... ALL weapons are the ones marked@with ALL...
And MAP weapons are marked with MAP...@and the ones with no mark are Normal, right?
Correct. An attack with a Normal weapon@is called a Normal Attack...
An attack with an ALL weapon is an ALL Attack,@and an attack with a MAP weapon is called@a MAP Weapon.
A Normal Attack weapon damages one unit,@while an ALL Attack weapon damages a whole@squad...
And a MAP Weapon damages every squad@within its area of effect.
Th-that's powerful!
Also, keep in mind that position matchups@matter in combat.
Same positions--your main unit attacking the@enemy's main unit, or sub attacking sub--@are fine, but...
Opposite positions--such as a main unit@attacking a sub unit--deal less damage@than normal.
Attacks from the main unit deal 100% damage@to the enemy's main unit and 65% to its sub.
I see...
Also, some weapons can only be used when@the pilot's Will is at a certain level@or higher.
Will also affects the damage you deal.@It rises and falls as you fight in battles@and as enemy or allied units are shot down.
Now, I'll demonstrate an ALL Attack.
So that's an ALL Attack...
Some ALL Attack weapons can also perform@a Double Attack, damaging an adjacent enemy@squad at the same time.
Next, I'll explain MAP Weapons.
Yes, sir.
As I said earlier, MAP Weapons damage every@squad within their area of effect.
Their damage isn't reduced by position,@and the enemy can't counterattack.
That's pretty handy!
However, if allies are within the area,@they'll take damage along with the enemy.
Be very careful when using MAP Weapons.
Y-Yes, ma'am.
Now, I'll use a MAP Weapon for real.
Wh-whoa... wiped 'em all out in one go.
One feature of MAP Weapons is that each type@has its own unique area of effect.
Next, I'll explain Normal Attacks.
Huh? There's more than one kind of@Normal Attack?
That's right. In battles between Twin Units,@you can choose Single Attack or Focused Attack.@I'll explain each one briefly.
First, Single Attack. With this, each of the@Twin Unit's two units attacks its target...@the enemy in the same position.
Use Single Attack when you want to spread@damage evenly across an enemy squad.
Understood!
Now, I'll explain Focused Attack.
Single Attack hits the enemy in the same@position, while Focused Attack lets you pick@any one unit in the enemy squad to attack.
So I can gang up on whoever's in the way!
Exactly. Now, I'll demonstrate@a Focused Attack.
That was a Focused Attack. Remember that@Normal Attacks come in two kinds:@Single Attack and Focused Attack.
Also, Normal Attacks can trigger Support@Attack or Support Defense from adjacent squads.
With Support Attack, an adjacent squad makes@a follow-up attack after your Normal Attack.
Conversely, with Support Defense, when the@enemy hits you with a Normal Attack,@an adjacent squad takes the damage instead.
I see... So with a Normal Attack,@the unit next to me might lend a hand.
That's right, but you can't always@perform a Support Attack.
To perform a "Support Attack" or "Support Defense,"@the main pilot needs the special skill@"Support Attack Lv" or "Support Defense Lv."
Got it!@I'll pick that stuff up as I play!
Besides the attacks I've covered, there are@other types, such as Combination Attacks@and Maximum Break.
A Combination Attack uses a dedicated@Combination Attack weapon to hit@up to five enemies at once.
Weapons marked with a C are the ones@that can be used for Combination Attacks.
Also, the targets must be next to each other,@and the attacking pilot must have learned the@special skill Continuous Attack Lv.
If "Twin Units" are adjacent and the attacking@pilot has learned the special skill "MB Activate,"@they can perform a "Maximum Break."
In a Maximum Break, four units unleash@a barrage with support weapons marked F,@followed by an attack with the main weapon.
Note that weapons marked ALL can't@be used as the main weapon.
Also, everyone's Will must be 140 or higher.@And afterward, their Will drops by 10.@So think carefully about when to use it.
The key to victory is using the attacks I've@taught you as the situation demands.
Normal Attack, ALL Attack,@and, uh... what was the other one?
I already told you what to do at times like this.
Huh? What was it again?
Seriously... I taught you that first thing.
Oh, right!@I press <I=92>!
Next lesson: looking up terms on the Status@screen and elsewhere... using Menu Help.
Using Status in the Unit Commands lets you@see all sorts of info about that unit.
Arado, bring up the help for the weapon@types we just talked about.
Uhh, I open "Stats" in the "Individual Commands"...@and press <I=92> on the "Weapon Stats" screen.
I see... Help can tell you all kinds of stuff.
Also, <I=92> Help can be used while the@"General Commands" or "Individual Commands"@are displayed.
In that case, a description of the command@appears at the bottom of the screen.
When in trouble, <I=92> Help!
You earn EXP by hitting@or shooting down enemies.
Every 500 EXP, the pilot levels up@and grows stronger.
You can also earn EXP by using@the Repair or Resupply commands.
Repair? Resupply?
They're special commands that@support other units in combat.
Only certain units can use them...@but if you don't master them, you won't@win the tough battles.
If a unit with that ability is made squad@leader, the command will appear@in the Unit Commands.
For example, after taking damage from@an enemy attack...
Ah!
I'll set the Mass-Production Huckebein Mk-II@equipped with a Repair Module as the main unit.
Whoa! My HP recovered!
That was Repair.
Then what about Resupply?
Resupply restores a unit's spent EN@and weapon ammo.
Keep in mind both commands only work on@squads within Repair or Resupply range.
Shooting down enemies also earns Funds and PP,@and sometimes even Enhancement Parts.
Those are used during the Intermission@after you clear a map.
All right!@First, I'll beat the enemies and clear the map!
The enemy will fight back, so be careful.
Now, let's begin the final lesson.
Clear this one, and you'll be ready@to start the game right away.
Yeah! I beat the enemies!
Good. You've mastered the basics.
I won this time, but I bet there are@some tough maps out there.@Think I can clear them?
Dammit, I got taken out!
Normally, that'd be a Game Over.
Aw, man... What do I do?
No need to worry.@On a Game Over, you restart the map@from the beginning, but...
The Funds and EXP you earned before the@Game Over carry over.
So if I level up and then get a Game Over,@I get to retry at that level?
That's right.@Even tough maps can be cleared if you keep at it.
Then I've got nothing to worry about!
There's also a Strategy Q&A with tips@and info to help you beat the game.
Reading it should help when you're@tackling difficult maps.
So how do I view that?
Select "LIBRARY" on the title screen,@then select "Strategy Q&A"...
Or go to "Library" under "Options" during@the "Intermission" and pick "Strategy Q&A."
That concludes the battle map guidance.
Good work, Arado.
That was a piece of cake!@So, is this the "Intermission"?
No. The "Intermission" comes once this@"Scenario Demo" is over.
That's where you prepare to move on to the@next scenario.
Prepare?
For example, you can save your game@data up to this point...
Reorganize your team for the next scenario,@equip your units with "Enhancement Parts"...
Upgrade units with "Funds" earned in battle,@and train pilots using "PP."
I see.
To really understand it, you should see an@actual "Intermission" in the main story.@Then try out the various functions yourself.
Roger that!@Then I'll jump right into the main story!
But first, a quick review.@What should you do if something confuses you?
Uhh... umm... Oh, I know!
First, I find some way to call Major Kai!
Yes. Then I appear on the screen and give@you the answer...
You fool! There's no such feature!!
Aww, man...@You players out there know the answer, right?
With that, the "Guidance Scenario" is complete.@I wish you all luck, players. Until we meet@again in the main story.
